failure_mode: catheter flow dysfunction: inability to sustain the prescribed extracorporeal blood flow rate
failure: Documented nephrology-access problem: tunneled cuffed hemodialysis catheters in service frequently fail to sustain the prescribed extracorporeal blood flow (commonly prescribed in the 300-400 mL/min range in the literature), forcing prolonged treatment time or under-dialysis. Documented mechanisms include fibrin sheath formation around the catheter tip, tip malposition or wall apposition inside the vein, kinking of the tunnel segment, and lumen thrombus; interventions in practice include thrombolytic locks, sheath stripping, and catheter exchange. Literature reports measurable recirculation and arterial/venous pressure derangements accompanying low-flow dysfunction. This description is qualitative problem-domain context from the clinical and bioengineering literature; no specific incidence rates are asserted here (the engine's own retrieval must find and custody the evidence).
constraint: Any intervention must sustain prescribed blood flow at extracorporeal pressures the pump circuit tolerates, without increasing recirculation of dialyzed blood, without increasing infection risk at the exit site or inside the tunnel, and without requiring a different insertion technique than standard tunneled catheter placement.

sources.problem_basis: clinical-literature qualitative context; no fabricated incidence counts
